reproduction_target: A purely computational resource paper. The target is: (a) training the previously published epigenome-ssm non-negative state-space model on 9,539 ChromImpute-imputed histone-modification ChIP-seq bigWig tracks downloaded from the IHEC repository (hg38, 25 bp bins, six core marks, 1,698 biosamples), trained on the ENCODE Pilot regions (1% of the genome, liftOver'd hg19 -> hg38, ENCODE exclusion-list regions removed), yielding K=33 (and K=16) continuous pan-cell-type chromatin state features genome-wide; (b) a set of quantitative evaluations comparing those features against four alternative pan-cell-type annotations (DHS-NMF, Sei, Universal ChromHMM 100-label, CSREP discrete + continuous) by linear-regression prediction of RNA-seq TPM (gene body and 2 kb TSS window), FANTOM5 CAGE enhancer activity, and phyloP conservation; (c) feature-enrichment analyses against GENCODE v45 elements, ENCODE SCREEN cCREs, CpG islands, RepeatMasker, FANTOM5 enhancers and DHSs; (d) feature-to-cell-type and feature-to-GO-term association by matrix products; (e) manual assignment of feature mnemonics; and (f) a conservation-associated activity score (SSM-CAAS) from a non-negative linear regression predicting |phyloP| from the features, plus GWAS Catalog variant enrichment of that score. There is no wet-lab component: all input data were generated by other consortia (IHEC / ChromImpute imputations produced by the Ernst Lab).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list taken from section '4 Methods' (subsections 4.1 Input data and processing, 4.2 epigenome-ssm model/training/annotation pipeline, 4.3 Alternative pan-cell type annotations, 4.4 Gene expression prediction, 4.5 Enhancer activity prediction, 4.6 Evolutionary conservation prediction, 4.7 Enrichment of pan-cell type features for annotated genomic elements, 4.8 Associating features with cell types through gene expression, 4.9 Associating features with GO terms, 4.10 Assigning feature mnemonics, 4.11 Conservation-associated activity score, 4.12 Enrichment for GWAS variants), plus one step (C6, feature-count selection by elbow method) whose only description lives in Results section 2.1 rather than Methods. Section cross-references inside the Methods text are inconsistent in the preprint (Methods 4.x subsections are cross-referenced as 'section 5.x'); this is a copy-editing artifact, not a scoring issue. The full availability statement is section '5 Code and data availability', quoted verbatim: 'Here is a link to a UCSC genome browser session containing the pan-cell type feature tracks along with the SSM-CAAS track: https://genome.ucsc.edu/s/habib/epigenome%2Dssm.IHEC.compact Also, the latest code for the epigenome-ssm pipeline can be found here: https://github.com/habibdanesh/epigenome-ssm'. Only the repository LANDING page and README prose (plus the README-referenced environment.yaml, read as a declared manifest, not as workflow source) were consulted, per stage-1 rules; no workflow source was read. Routed pure-computational rather than tool-methods because epigenome-ssm itself was published in 2022 (Daneshpajouh et al., Bioinformatics 38(11):3029-3036) and this paper applies it to produce a resource, although the repository is also the tool's own distribution, which gives the routing a tool-methods flavour.

steps.label: Download 9,539 bigWig tracks of -log10 p-value signal for six core histone-modification ChIP-seq assays from the IHEC repository; these are ChromImpute imputations at 25 bp resolution derived from 5,339 observed ChIP-seq tracks across 1,698 biosamples. No accession, EpiRR identifier, IHEC data-release version, download date, track manifest or ChromImpute version is given, and no URL for the IHEC repository appears in the paper.

Transform all input signals with the inverse hyperbolic sine, arcsinh(x) = log(x + sqrt(x^2 + 1)), to reduce outlier influence; performed inside the Snakemake data-preparation stage of the public epigenome-ssm pipeline.

Convert the ENCODE Pilot regions (1% of the human genome, used as the training regions) from hg19 to hg38 with the UCSC liftOver tool. No liftOver version, no chain file identity or version, and no command-line options (minMatch etc.) are stated; the repository ships only the already-lifted output BED (data/misc/encodePilotRegions.hg38.liftover.bed), not the conversion step.

Remove the ENCODE exclusion-list regions from all analyses; the annotation regions file is the complement of the exclusion list. The paper cites the exclusion list only by reference [39]; the accession ENCFF356LFX appears only in the repository README (data/misc/ENCFF356LFX_complement.bed), not in the paper prose.

Train the epigenome-ssm non-negative state-space model by expectation maximization: emission matrix Z (E x K) and transition matrix T (K x K), objective J(Z,T) = log P(alpha, Z, T | Y) + lambda_1 ||Z||_F + lambda_2 ||T||_F, non-negativity enforced by an active-set method of Lagrange multipliers, ten random parameter initializations with the best log-likelihood retained, and no fixed iteration count ('we kept the training going until there was no significant improvement in log-likelihood'). The values of lambda_1 and lambda_2, the convergence threshold, max_iter, n_chunks, bin_size actually used, and the random seeds are not stated in the paper.

Feature-count selection (described only in Results 2.1, not in Methods): train the model with 50 features, sort features by total emission value, and apply 'an elbow method' to drop the 17 lowest-emission features, retaining K=33; a K=16 model is also compared throughout. No elbow criterion, threshold, or implementing script is given, and this meta-procedure over pipeline runs is not part of the deposited Snakemake workflow.

Apply the trained model to generate whole-genome continuous feature annotations, then normalize each feature i so its genome-wide mean is 1 and multiply the corresponding emission column Z[:,i] by the unnormalized genome-wide mean. Outputs (.npy and bigWig feature tracks) are distributed only as a UCSC Genome Browser session, with no bulk download, DOI or repository deposit.

Obtain the four alternative pan-cell-type annotations used as comparators: DHS-NMF (DHS coordinates [40] and NMF components [41], the latter a Zenodo file URL), Sei sequence classes (a BED file from an S3 URL [42]), Universal ChromHMM (100-label model, downloaded from the IHEC repository, generated by the Ernst Lab), and CSREP (56 discrete BED files plus 1,008 CSREP-con bigWig files of 18-label probabilities across 56 sample groups, also from the IHEC repository). The Zenodo and S3 items carry direct URLs; the two IHEC-hosted annotation sets carry no accession, version or download date.

Gene expression prediction benchmark: download RNA-seq TPM for 1,467 epigenomes from the IHEC repository; build per-gene predictor vectors from each annotation (K averaged feature values for epigenome-ssm; length-100 coverage-weighted one-hot for Universal ChromHMM; length-18 per sample group for CSREP-dis and probabilities for CSREP-con; length-40 for Sei; length-16 for DHS-NMF), over the gene body and, separately, a 2 kb window centred on the annotated TSS; arcsinh-transform predictors and response; fit scikit-learn LinearRegression under 10-fold cross-validation; score with Pearson and Spearman correlation. Restricted to protein-coding genes using GENCODE v45. No scikit-learn version, no CV seed, and no accession for the IHEC RNA-seq matrix.

Enhancer activity prediction benchmark: download FANTOM5 CAGE TPM data for 1,827 samples [45] and FANTOM5 enhancer annotations [46], liftOver the coordinates hg19 -> hg38, extract annotations overlapping enhancers as predictors, arcsinh-transform predictors and response, and fit the same cross-validated linear regression. No FANTOM5 release version or download date, no liftOver version or chain file, no seed.

Evolutionary conservation prediction benchmark: download the UCSC Genome Browser phyloP track generated from multiple alignments of 99 vertebrate genomes to human [47], restrict the analysis to DHSs (because DHS-NMF is defined only there), use the mean absolute phyloP score per DHS as the response, arcsinh-transform both sides, and fit the same cross-validated linear regression. The track is identified by description rather than by a versioned file name or download date.

Enrichment of each pan-cell-type feature for annotated genomic elements, computed as mean feature value over the regions divided by the feature's genome-wide mean. Element sets: GENCODE v45 protein-coding genes (TSS, TTS, TSS +/- 1 kb, CDS, five_prime_UTR, three_prime_UTR, exon; introns obtained with the bedtools subtract command [48]; zinc-finger genes by gene_name containing 'ZNF'; pseudogenes by gene_type containing 'pseudogene'), ENCODE SCREEN cCREs (PLS, pELS, dELS, DNase-H3K4me3, CTCF-only), CpG islands [51] and RepeatMasker regions [52] from the UCSC Genome Browser, FANTOM5 enhancers [46], and the DHS coordinates [40]. No bedtools version, no SCREEN/CpG/RepeatMasker release or download date.

Associate features with cell types: build a feature-by-gene matrix (mean feature value at protein-coding genes) and a cell-type-by-gene RNA-seq expression matrix from 1,467 IHEC epigenomes, and take their product over the gene axis to obtain a feature-by-cell-type matrix; features are then summarized over 12 high-level and 40 intermediate cell ontologies. The biosample-to-ontology mapping table is not deposited and no accession is given for the RNA-seq matrix.

Associate features with Gene Ontology terms: build a feature-by-gene matrix and a GO-term-by-gene binary matrix, take the product over the gene axis, include all terms assigned to each gene except terms assigned to fewer than 30 genes. GO data files were 'downloaded from [55, 56]' with no release identifier, ontology/annotation file name, or download date; GO is a rolling resource.

Assign a mnemonic to each pan-cell-type feature by manual curation: activity component from feature enrichment around public annotations (GENCODE, ENCODE, FANTOM, DHS) combined with high emission for the relevant histone marks, with a feature counted as enriched if its mean value over the annotated regions is >= 2; cell-type component from ranking input tracks by emission and computing the proportion of total emission per 12 high-level and per 40 intermediate ontologies, then applying judgment rules ('unless a dominant intermediate ontology was supported by both the gene expression and GO analyses', higher-order labels for related types, 'SG' when unrelated, 'Broad' when ungroupable). No script implements this and the decision inputs (Table 1, Figs. 3, 4, S8) are not deposited in machine-readable form.

Conservation-associated activity score (SSM-CAAS): train a non-negative linear regression taking the pan-cell-type features as input and predicting the absolute phyloP score per genomic bin, using 5-fold cross-validation and the average coefficients as the final model, then emit a genome-wide predicted-phyloP track. The solver/library for the non-negative regression, the bin size used, the regularization (if any), and the CV seed are not stated.

GWAS variant enrichment of SSM-CAAS: download disease-associated variants from the GWAS Catalog [57], sort genomic bins by SSM-CAAS (and separately by phyloP), count GWAS variants covered by each bin, and plot fold enrichment over the genome-wide average. No GWAS Catalog release or download date, no trait filtering or p-value threshold, no bin size restated, no deposited script.

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 4/17 (23.5%). The four RI steps (C2 arcsinh transform, C4 exclusion-list removal, C5 SSM training, C7 whole-genome annotation + normalization) are exactly the steps executed by the public Snakemake pipeline at https://github.com/habibdanesh/epigenome-ssm, whose README declares a conda environment.yaml; that manifest names seven dependencies (snakemake, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn, ucsc-bigwigaverageoverbed, ucsc-bedgraphpack, ucsc-bedgraphtobigwig) with zero version constraints, no interpreter pin and no platform declaration, so the version axis caps at 1 (subtier floating) and R-star is unreachable for them from prose. The remaining 13 steps fall to NI: every downstream evaluation (C9-C17) is described in prose only, with no deposited analysis code, no software versions (scikit-learn, bedtools, liftOver are named without versions) and, for GO, GWAS Catalog, SCREEN, CpG islands, RepeatMasker, FANTOM5 and phyloP, no release identifier or download date. GENCODE v45 is the single explicitly pinned reference release in the whole paper. Note also the under-claim direction required by the rubric: a 0 static_readiness is a bounded statement about declared state, not evidence that the pipeline would fail to run.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (16 from section 4 Methods, 1 from Results 2.1); 0 wet-lab steps - the study is purely computational and reuses data generated by IHEC and imputations generated by the Ernst Lab at UCLA. The paper has a combined availability statement (section 5 'Code and data availability') that supplies exactly two URLs: a UCSC Genome Browser session and the epigenome-ssm GitHub repository, referenced as 'the latest code' with no tag, release or commit. Both resolve (200). The study's own primary output - the pan-cell-type feature tracks and the SSM-CAAS track across 1,698 biosamples - is distributed only through that browser session; there is no bulk download, DOI, Zenodo deposit or accession for it. The input data are attributed to 'the IHEC repository' with no URL, accession, EpiRR identifier or data-release version anywhere in the paper.

gaps.where: All 17 computational steps. Paper prose: no version number appears for any software (epigenome-ssm, ChromImpute, UCSC liftOver, bedtools, scikit-learn, Snakemake, numpy). Repository: environment.yaml (read as a declared manifest from the README instructions) at https://github.com/habibdanesh/epigenome-ssm.
gaps.missing: 2a for the prose: not one software version is stated in the paper. 2b for the repository: environment.yaml declares channels conda-forge and bioconda and seven dependencies - snakemake, numpy, matplotlib, seaborn, ucsc-bigwigaverageoverbed, ucsc-bedgraphpack, ucsc-bedgraphtobigwig - with no version constraint on any of them, no python/interpreter pin, no platform declaration, and no lockfile. The repository has zero tags and zero releases (GitHub API, checked 2026-07-28), and the paper points at 'the latest code', i.e. a moving default branch; the branch has been pushed to since the preprint (last push 2026-05-27). scikit-learn and bedtools, which the Methods do use, are not even present in the declared environment.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock or pixi lock (or a container image referenced by digest) covering the declared platform and interpreter, add the missing analysis dependencies (scikit-learn, bedtools) to the manifest, and cite an immutable release tag / Zenodo-archived snapshot of the repository from the paper instead of 'the latest code'.

gaps.where: Steps C6 and C9-C17: feature-count selection, all five benchmark/evaluation analyses, both matrix-product association analyses, the mnemonic assignment, the CAAS regression, and the GWAS enrichment.
gaps.missing: The deposited Snakemake workflow covers only data preparation, model training and annotation (README: 'handles data preparation, model training, and annotation automatically through a single Snakemake workflow'). None of the evaluation code is deposited: no script for the elbow-based feature pruning, no regression/benchmark code for the gene-expression, CAGE and phyloP predictions or the one-hot encodings of the comparator annotations, no enrichment code, no feature-by-cell-type and feature-by-GO matrix code, no CAAS training code, no GWAS enrichment code, and no figure-generating code for Figs. 2-5 and the supplementary figures.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit an analysis repository (or an analysis/ subdirectory of the existing repo) containing the benchmark, enrichment, association, CAAS and figure scripts, and archive it with a DOI at the version used for the paper.

gaps.where: Steps C8, C10, C11, C12, C14, C17 - every external reference resource except GENCODE.
gaps.missing: Reference resources are cited by publication or by bare URL with no release identifier or download date: GO data files 'downloaded from [55, 56]' (GO is re-released continuously), the GWAS Catalog [57], ENCODE SCREEN cCREs [49, 50], CpG islands [51] and RepeatMasker [52] from UCSC, FANTOM5 CAGE [45] and enhancers [46], the phyloP 99-vertebrate track [47], and the Universal ChromHMM and CSREP annotation sets pulled from the IHEC repository. Only two references carry a directly versioned artifact URL (DHS-NMF components on Zenodo record 3838751, Sei sequence classes on S3), and only GENCODE is pinned to a release (v45). Because the pipeline takes user-supplied local paths for all inputs, none of these are fetched by pinned rules in the workflow either - though the definitive A/B/C classification is a Stage-2 code check and is deliberately left n/a here.
gaps.how_to_close: State the release identifier and download date for every external resource (GO release date, GWAS Catalog release, SCREEN/cCRE version, UCSC table dump dates, FANTOM5 phase/release, phyloP track file name, IHEC data-release version) and, where possible, add download rules that fetch a specific versioned artifact rather than expecting a local path.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C8, C9, C13 - the entire input side, plus the study's own output tracks (C7).
gaps.missing: No accession, EpiRR identifier, sample manifest, track list or IHEC data-release version is given for the 9,539 imputed bigWig tracks, the 5,339 observed ChIP-seq tracks they derive from, the 1,467 RNA-seq epigenomes, or the 1,698 biosamples; the paper does not even give a URL for 'the IHEC repository'. The biosample-to-cell-ontology mapping underlying the 12 high-level and 40 intermediate ontology groupings (central to Figs. 3, 4 and to the mnemonics) is not deposited. In the reverse direction, the study's own output - the pan-cell-type feature tracks and SSM-CAAS track - is reachable only through a UCSC Genome Browser session, with no bulk download, DOI or deposit, so a reproducer cannot compare their regenerated tracks against the published ones at the file level.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the exact input track manifest (IHEC/EpiRR accessions plus data-release version) and the biosample-to-ontology table as supplementary files, and deposit the output feature tracks and SSM-CAAS track (bigWig plus the emission matrix) under a DOI in addition to the browser session.

gaps.where: Steps C5 (ten random EM initializations), C6 (selection over those runs), C9-C11 (10-fold cross-validation), C16 (5-fold cross-validation).
gaps.missing: No random seed is reported anywhere. The model is trained from ten random initializations with the best log-likelihood retained, and training is stopped when there is 'no significant improvement in log-likelihood' with no threshold given, so neither the initialization draw nor the stopping point can be reproduced; likewise no seed is given for the cross-validation splits in the benchmark and CAAS analyses.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seeds (or the seed-generation rule) for the initializations and the CV splits, state the convergence threshold numerically, and note that in their absence agreement can only be assessed distributionally.

gaps.missing: Two decision procedures are described only in prose and have no implementation anywhere: the 'elbow method' used to drop 17 of 50 features (no criterion, no threshold, no plot-generating script) and the mnemonic-assignment procedure, which mixes a quantitative rule (mean feature value over annotated regions >= 2) with explicit human judgment ('unless a dominant intermediate ontology was supported by both the gene expression and GO analyses', 'when several closely related cell types were dominant, we used a higher-order label'). Table 1 and the underlying per-feature emission/expression/GO evidence are not provided in machine-readable form.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the pruning script with an explicit numeric criterion, and publish the per-feature evidence matrices plus the mnemonic decision table so that the curatorial step is at least auditable even where it is not mechanizable.

gaps.where: Steps C1 and C8 - the upstream imputation and comparator-annotation sub-pipelines.
gaps.missing: The primary inputs are ChromImpute imputations generated externally ('We would like to thank the Ernst Lab at UCLA for generating ChromImpute imputations'), and two of the four comparator annotation sets (Universal ChromHMM with 100 labels, CSREP with 18 states over 56 sample groups) were likewise generated by the Ernst Lab and merely downloaded from the IHEC repository. No version, parameter set, or run record is given for any of these external sub-pipelines, and the paper explicitly notes that its Universal ChromHMM annotations are 'similar, but not identical' to the published ones. A reproducer therefore cannot regenerate the study's inputs or its comparators, only re-download them if they remain hosted.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact IHEC release and per-track identifiers for the imputed signal and the ChromHMM/CSREP annotation sets, with the ChromImpute and ChromHMM versions and parameter files used to produce them, so that the externalized sub-pipelines are at least identifiable.
